claims.text: Adding 0.1–1 at.% titanium followed by controlled annealing will refine the grain structure of MnNiSi-based alloys.
Titanium microalloying followed by controlled annealing will improve the mechanical performance of MnNiSi-based alloys.
The intervention will retain a large magnetocaloric effect.
The as-synthesized polycrystalline MnNiSi-based baseline has relatively coarse grains.
Controlled annealing of the titanium-containing alloy will form nanostructured precipitates.
Annealing near the dissolution point followed by moderate cooling rates is suitable for the proposed intervention.
Keeping titanium within 0.1–1 at.% will avoid materially altering the magnetic transitions.
Nano- to microscale precipitates will impede dislocation movement.
Titanium will act as a nucleation site during heat treatment.
Titanium-assisted nucleation will promote grain refinement and precipitate formation.
The refined microstructure will increase yield strength by inhibiting dislocation mobility.
The refined microstructure will improve fracture toughness by inhibiting dislocation mobility.
The titanium-modified microstructure will maintain the magnetic ordering and phase transitions responsible for the magnetocaloric effect.
The doped and annealed material will have higher yield strength and fracture toughness than the undoped baseline.
The magnetocaloric effect will be reduced by less than 10% relative to the undoped baseline.
The intervention is effective only within a titanium concentration range of 0.1–1 at.%.
Exceeding 1 at.% titanium or substantially changing the annealing conditions may degrade magnetocaloric properties or cause unexpected phase transformations.
Specific experimental support for the intervention in MnNiSi-based magnetic-refrigeration materials is lacking.
